transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood Solutions); Dr. Priya Shah (CISO, Medivault), Liam O'Connor (Cloud Architect), Maya Li (Legal), Samir Patel (Product)

Summary:
Quick security/compliance review focused on data residency and region pinning (US/EU), cross-border processing, and sub-processor disclosures. Confirmed high-level capabilities: per-customer region pinning, private control plane options, KMS integration, and audit logging. Customer asked about encrypted at-rest keys, BYOK, SOC2/ISO evidence, sub-processor list and contractual obligations. Agreed next steps to share SOC2/ISO docs and schedule region pinning demo in sandbox.

Topics:
- Data residency / region pinning (US vs EU)
- Cross-border processing & lawful basis
- Sub-processors and contractual commitments
- Encryption/KMS & BYOK
- Audit logs and retention
- RBAC / SSO integration notes

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone thanks for making time, um I'm Ethan with Redwood, I'll kick us off. Sofia and Jordan are here from our security/solutions group.
[00:12] Dr. Priya Shah: Thanks Ethan, yeah we just want to make sure there's no cross-border processing for certain PHI-ish flows, we're in healthcare, so residency and sub-processors are big for us.
[00:22] Sofia Martinez: Totally understood. Quick confirmation question - are you planning to use Hosted API or Dedicated / Private deployment for this workload? That drives options.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Initially hosted, but we may move to Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private if required. For now we need to ensure data for EU patients stays in EU, and US data stays in US, and no tokens or logs leave region.
[00:45] Jordan Li: Right. On Hosted we offer region pinning per-customer - you can pin requests to eu-west-1 or us-east-1. There's also a Private option where the control plane sits in your VPC and data never crosses.
[01:02] Dr. Priya Shah: When you say "pinning" is that at the request level, or per-model, or per-customer? We have multi-tenant app but need tenant-level pinning.
[01:15] Sofia Martinez: Good question. We do tenant-level pinning via route configs. So you can route tenants to a specific region and model variant. It's not just global per-account. There is a small note - if a fallback happens due to capacity we will only fall back to a compatible model in the same region unless you opt into cross-region fallback.
[01:36] Samir Patel: Can you spell out that fallback option? Like if eu capacity is saturated, will requests go to us and does that require consent?
[01:44] Ethan Park: By default we don't cross-region. Cross-region fallback is an explicit policy you can enable; we log it and surface it in audit logs and you can set automatic deny. For regulated workloads we usually recommend Dedicated or Private to avoid that risk.
[02:05] Maya Li: On contract terms we need sub-processor list and assurances - what's your current sub-processor roster and how often is it updated?
[02:15] Jordan Li: We maintain a sub-processor list; most common are major cloud infra providers and a few monitoring services. We'll share the current list and weekly updates. We'll include the legal data processing addendum and standard SCCs if needed.
[02:30] Liam O'Connor: About encryption - KMS integration - do you support BYOK? Our security policy requires customer-managed keys for production PHI.
[02:40] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we support KMS integration and BYOK in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration endpoints - you can bring keys from AWS KMS, Google KMS, or Azure Key Vault, and we encrypt at rest. Small caveat: some edge caches, like the prefix cache, are encrypted but the key lifetime policies should be discussed.
[03:05] Dr. Priya Shah: Is the KMS held in the same region as the data? We need to ensure keys are region-bound.
[03:12] Jordan Li: Keys are region-scoped for all major providers; if you pin to eu-west-1 you'd use eu KMS region. For Private deployments you can use an on-prem HSM as well.
[03:25] Ethan Park: Also to call out - audit logs capture request metadata, region, model version, and policy triggers. Payload logging is configurable and we can disable full payload retention for PHI.
[03:38] Samir Patel: How long do logs persist by default?
[03:41] Sofia Martinez: Default is 90 days in the console, but for enterprise we support longer retention or export to your SIEM. For compliance we can set up streaming to your Splunk/Datadog or an S3 bucket in your region.
[03:55] Liam O'Connor: If we export to S3, will data be encrypted server-side and use our KMS?
[04:01] Jordan Li: Yes, server-side encryption with customer-managed keys is supported for export buckets.
[04:07] Dr. Priya Shah: A few compliance specifics - do you have SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001 certifications?
[04:14] Ethan Park: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 - we'll share the attestation documents and control mappings.
[04:21] Maya Li: Great. Please include the scope - does SOC2 include the hosted inference plane?
[04:27] Sofia Martinez: The report covers the hosted control plane and core infra. For Dedicated and Private we provide additional runbooks and architecture diagrams. We'll mark scope in the package.
[04:38] Dr. Priya Shah: About cross-border processing - what about sub-processors that may replicate telemetry outside EU for redundancy?
[04:46] Jordan Li: We try to avoid cross-region replication for EU-data pinned customers. Some non-sensitive telemetry may be aggregated across regions, but for pinned customers we'd turn that off and route telemetry to the pinned region. We'll show config options in the demo.
[05:01] Samir Patel: Any gotchas with model variants and quantization - does model compilation ever require sending weights to another region?
[05:10] Sofia Martinez: No, model weights are stored in the region where the model variant is provisioned. For managed model updates we replicate artifacts using encrypted pipelines, but that replication can be limited to chosen regions.
[05:25] Dr. Priya Shah: We need an explicit statement that metadata about tenant routing won't leave the EU.
[05:31] Ethan Park: Affirmative - for tenant-level pinned accounts we can keep routing metadata in-region and show you the audit trail.
[05:38] Liam O'Connor: Authentication - SSO and RBAC. We will want SCIM + SAML and fine-grained roles so only ops can change pinning.
[05:48] Jordan Li: We support SAML 2.0 SSO + SCIM for provisioning and RBAC with custom roles. You can lock down who can change routing policies.
[05:58] Maya Li: Is there an admin audit trail for RBAC changes?
[06:01] Sofia Martinez: Yes - admin actions are logged with who/when/what and exported to your SIEM or available via the console.
[06:08] Dr. Priya Shah: Can we get a short technical section on the fallback logic and the exact log fields captured? Our auditors will want to see field list.
[06:16] Ethan Park: We'll include that. It has the timestamp, request id, tenant id, region pin status, fallback indicators, model version, and policy id. We'll drop the log schema.
[06:27] Samir Patel: Any third-party sub-processors in the EU specifically?
[06:31] Jordan Li: A handful - e.g., eu-based logging and monitoring partners, and cloud infra in eu-west-1. We'll provide the list and contracts.
[06:39] Dr. Priya Shah: About contractual remedies - can you add standard DPA with SCCs or adopt EU data adequacy clauses?
[06:47] Ethan Park: Yes we provide a DPA, SCCs, and we can work with your legal team on any redlines.
[06:52] Liam O'Connor: Network architecture question - do you provide private connectivity options like AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering for Dedicated?
[06:59] Jordan Li: For Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering and PrivateLink connections. For Hosted we support customer-controlled egress and proxying via our private connectors.
[07:13] Maya Li: On sub-processor notification - what's the SLA for notifying customers of changes?
[07:18] Sofia Martinez: We notify customers 30 days ahead for major sub-processor changes, and immediate notification if it affects security posture.
[07:26] Samir Patel: Performance question - will pinning to eu-west-1 add latency for US users?
[07:33] Ethan Park: If end-users are in US but you pin compute to EU you'll see RTT impact. Usually customers route tenants geographically to match users. We can run a latency benchmark as part of the POC.
[07:46] Samir Patel: Could you show us the latency numbers?
[07:49] Sofia Martinez: We'll include some benchmark spreadsheets in the follow-up and can run a short scoped perf run in the sandbox.
[07:58] Dr. Priya Shah: How about cross-border legal basis - does Redwood ever process EU data in the US for troubleshooting?
[08:06] Jordan Li: By default no for pinned accounts. For troubleshooting we can request consent and perform controlled access with limited logs and an audit. We also support session recordings only with explicit approvals.
[08:19] Maya Li: Ok, that helps. For legal signoff we'll need the SOC2, ISO, DPA, sub-processor list, and an explicit region pinning architecture doc.
[08:28] Ethan Park: We'll bundle all that.
[08:31] Q&A rapid fire:
[08:31] [00:10] Liam O'Connor: Do you support customer-managed keys in eu-west-1 for hosted?
[08:35] [00:12] Sofia Martinez: Yes.
[08:37] [00:14] Dr. Priya Shah: Can we turn off any cross-region telemetry?
[08:39] [00:16] Jordan Li: Yes, per-tenant telemetry is configurable.
[08:42] [00:19] Samir Patel: How often do you update sub-processor list?
[08:44] [00:21] Ethan Park: Weekly and on-change alerts for customers.
[08:47] [00:24] Maya Li: Who signs the DPA?
[08:49] [00:26] Ethan Park: We'll provide standard DPA and signatories - we can work with your legal team.
[08:52] [00:29] Dr. Priya Shah: One more - do you have penetration test reports?
[08:56] [00:33] Sofia Martinez: Yes we have periodic pentest reports and an external vendor attestation; will include summary in the package.
[09:03] Ethan Park: Great - recap and next steps. We'll send the SOC2/ISO pack, sub-processor list, DPA + SCCs, region pinning architecture doc, and a sandbox invite for a short demo with region pinning enabled. Sofia will run a latency bench.
[09:20] Dr. Priya Shah: Perfect. Please mark the documents with scope and region details.
[09:24] Ethan Park: Will do. Thanks everyone.

References / Links mentioned:

End of transcript.
